clue.text: They are charged for half portions

indicators.note: half of the word portions is taken, here its back four letters

explanation.surface: Diners are billed for serving sizes that are only half as big.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the back half of PORTIONS. 'Charged' looks like being billed, but it means carrying an electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Atoms or molecules carrying an electric charge are ions in chemistry.

clue.text: Not well to repeat that one lacks education

parts.note: not well means ill
to repeat means to iterate

explanation.surface: Someone feeling unwell is told to repeat a lesson, being poorly schooled.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who cannot read or write is called an illiterate, someone without schooling.

clue.text: I'm on the way up with round article for her

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the run of pieces is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, I'm gives IM
O is round in shape
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone rising in the world with a well-rounded essay written for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' turns the whole run IMOAN round, since this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a woman's name, so a female pronoun can stand for it.

clue.text: Measure one encountered in the middle?

indicators.note: in tells us the next pieces go inside the word for the middle

parts.note: the middle is the centre
one is the Roman numeral I
encountered means met

explanation.surface: A question about the person you bumped into halfway along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts IMET inside CENTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A centimetre is a unit of length, a hundredth of a metre.

clue.text: Eat a lot, turn green and go inside

indicators.note: inside says the word go is placed within the rearranged letters
turn means the letters of green are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs themselves, feels sick, turns green and heads indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' looks like a change of colour, but it rearranges the colour word; 'inside' sets the other word within that scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge or cram oneself with food is to engorge.

clue.text: Aims to give better advice

parts.note: read 'better' as one who bets: the person described sets out to advise gamblers on racing

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to improve the counsel they offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like 'improved', but it is a noun: a person placing bets, whom a racing adviser serves.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing tipster sells predictions to gamblers about which horse will win.

clue.text: A month to live, possibly

parts.note: May is a month of the year
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A doctor's grim forecast: perhaps only thirty days left.
explanation.definitionFit: Perhaps, possibly and maybe are all adverbs of uncertainty.

clue.text: Lift vehicle on board? That's easily managed

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second
in a down clue, lift means the word is raised and so read upwards

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle
a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Loading a car onto a platform with a jack turns out to be no trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' turns CART into TRAC; 'on' sets it above TABLE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tractable is docile, compliant and simple to handle.

clue.text: Not difficult to be comfortable in this street

definitions.text: to be comfortable in this street
definitions.meaning: on ... Street, an idiom for a life of comfort and wealth

explanation.surface: Life is simple when you live comfortably on this road.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy means simple, and living on Easy Street is the idiom for prosperous comfort.

clue.text: Dismiss team at home

parts.note: to dismiss from a job is to fire
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A manager sacks the players while they are playing a home match.
explanation.definitionFit: The hearth stands for domestic life, so fireside means at home by the family hearth.

clue.text: Getting better employment as a researcher

definitions.meaning: improving, as things do when prospects rise
consulting references, the occupation of someone checking facts

explanation.surface: Things are improving now that I have landed a research job.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospects improving are said to be on the rise, and a researcher spends time checking words in reference books.

clue.text: Warm-hearted assent brought about after a long time

indicators.note: brought about here means placed around, so the word for assent surrounds the other piece

parts.note: yes is a word of assent

indicators.note: hearted points to the central letters, the heart, of warm

explanation.surface: A friendly agreement finally reached after long delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warm-hearted' reads as kindly, but '-hearted' takes the heart of 'Warm'; 'brought about' means wrapped around.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages, decades or years all describe a lengthy period.

clue.text: Note containing death-wish is nonsense

indicators.note: containing says the musical note holds the other piece within it

parts.note: te is a note of the tonic sol-fa scale
RIP, rest in peace, is the wish carved on gravestones

explanation.surface: A message revealing a suicidal urge is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: RIP (requiescat in pace) is the wish said over the dead, so 'death-wish' is read literally; 'containing' puts it inside the note.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is rubbish, worthless talk, in informal speech.

clue.text: Goes back and buys another round

definitions.meaning: treats the company again, standing drinks a second time

explanation.surface: A drinker returns to the bar and pays for the next round.
explanation.definitionFit: An army withdrawing is in retreat, and to re-treat friends is to stand them drinks again.

clue.text: Engineer Will Ross aboard finding jammed cylinders

annotationWithheld.why: 'Engineer Will Ross aboard finding jammed cylinders': the anagram of WILL ROSS goes inside SS, and 'aboard' is both the container signal and the only word for SS (steamship), one word doing two jobs, which the check refuses
annotationWithheld.clue: Engineer Will Ross aboard finding jammed cylinders

clue.text: Know how to convert into money

explanation.surface: Someone learns how to turn their possessions into cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp a truth is to become aware of it, and to cash in assets is to liquidate them.

clue.text: The humiliation of being put in a lower place

parts.note: a basement is a storey below ground

explanation.surface: Being demoted to a lowly position is a mortifying experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in a lower place' reads both as being demoted and, cryptically, as being placed in A BASEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Abasement is degradation, being brought low in dignity.

clue.text: Display of bright colours produced by artist in London area

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
taken as written
Bow is a district of east London

explanation.surface: A painter from the East End produces a vivid exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician; BOW is a district in London's East End.
explanation.definitionFit: The arc of spectral colours seen after rain shows a vivid band of hues.

clue.text: Elected to steal bananas, you said, going inside to become lag

parts.note: elected politicians are in, in office

indicators.note: going inside says the sound of you is placed within the rearranged letters
bananas means crazy, so the letters of steal are mixed up
said means the word you is heard, giving the single letter that sounds like it

parts.note: you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: A tale of political theft and a prisoner, with someone going inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' rearranges STEAL into SLATE, 'said' turns 'you' into U, and 'going inside' puts it after S. 'Lag' looks like a convict, but here means to wrap pipes against cold.
explanation.definitionFit: To lag pipes or a boiler is to wrap them in material that keeps heat in.

clue.text: An essay about old King Lear, for example

indicators.note: about here means around, so the attempt surrounds the other piece

parts.note: an essay is an attempt, a try
old means aged

explanation.surface: A student's paper on Shakespeare's elderly monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essay' looks like a school paper, but it means an attempt; 'about' wraps that attempt round the word for old.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's King Lear is a drama ending in catastrophe for its hero, a classic of the genre.

clue.text: Longed for time to take up study

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking up means the word is raised and read upwards

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room

explanation.surface: Someone eager for the chance to begin their studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take up' turns DEN into NED in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine or crave is to have yearned, a past tense of strong desire.

clue.text: They mail the bills

definitions.meaning: people who send letters by post

explanation.surface: Those who send out the invoices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bills' looks like invoices, but it means billboard notices.
explanation.definitionFit: People who send letters post them, and printed placards on walls are bills.

clue.text: Prince over North-Eastern Spain is a model of excellence

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: Aragon is a region of north-eastern Spain

explanation.surface: A royal ruling over a Spanish region is held up as perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a perfect example, a pattern of virtue.

clue.text: Suave and refined young lady broadcaster

parts.note: a deb, debutante, is a young society lady
being on air is broadcasting

explanation.surface: A polished, well-bred young woman who works on radio.
explanation.walkthrough: A DEB is a debutante, a young upper-class woman entering society.
explanation.definitionFit: A debonair man is urbane, charming and well-mannered.

clue.text: The sultan's subject — ought I to embrace the chap?

indicators.note: to embrace means the first pieces hold the other between them

parts.note: ought here is nought, zero, written O
taken as written
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A question about whether one should hug the fellow, asked of a ruler's subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ought' is an old form of nought, so O; 'to embrace' puts MAN between O and I. Oman is ruled by a sultan.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Oman, a sultanate, is a subject of its ruler.

clue.text: Scowl when let down

explanation.surface: Frowning when disappointed.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are said differently: one rhymes with 'power', the other with 'mower'.
explanation.definitionFit: To glower menacingly is one sense, and to drop something down is the other.

clue.text: Soft answer, diverting it

parts.note: an allusion to Proverbs 15:1, which says a soft answer turns away anger

explanation.surface: A gentle reply turns away the thing in question.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue quotes the Bible: 'A soft answer turneth away wrath'. 'it' is the thing that gets turned away.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbs names fury as what a gentle reply turns away.

clue.text: Game discovered by explorer

definitions.meaning: a sport played on horseback with mallets
Marco ..., the Venetian traveller to China

explanation.surface: A sport found by a famous traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: A mounted sport played with mallets shares its name with the Venetian traveller Marco.

clue.text: Work-time diversion

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Break time at the office is a welcome change.
explanation.walkthrough: OP is short for opus, a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening at the opera is entertainment, a pleasant amusement.

clue.text: Yield to temptation after dark, even?

definitions.text: Yield to temptation after dark, even?

parts.words: Yield to temptation after dark, even?
parts.note: read as night plus fall: to give in to temptation in the evening, and also simply the coming of dark

explanation.surface: Giving in to temptation once the lights are low.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'fall' is to yield to temptation, and to do it at 'night' is after dark; 'even' hints at evening, when that happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk, when darkness comes on, splits into night and the verb for sinning.

clue.text: By such means securing the lot

definitions.text: By such means securing the lot

parts.words: By such means securing the lot
parts.note: at an auction a lot is won by offering more than every rival

explanation.surface: This is how one wins everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the lot' looks like 'everything', but it is an auction lot.
explanation.definitionFit: At an auction, offering more than rivals wins the item for sale.

clue.text: Only one of these

parts.note: the clue's own last word is a plural pronoun, and its singular form is wanted

explanation.surface: Just a single item from the set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'these' is the plural; one of 'these' is the singular demonstrative pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: The singular of 'these' is the demonstrative used for one thing near at hand.
